request.prompt: Create a HAVENLINE World 1 authored crew upgrade concept sheet. Match the five supplied selected character references exactly in face, body proportions, hair/fur/feather pattern and scale relationships. The ONLY five actors are the referenced male survivor, referenced female survivor, referenced dog, referenced gray wolf and referenced owl. Chunky rounded stylized 3D, warm winter clothing, restrained blue metal and orange details, soft sculpted snow, clean navy studio setting. THREE large panels: two large group views across the top, a wide teamwork scene below. Top left is FRONT three-quarter, top right is the genuine opposite REAR three-quarter of the SAME outfits and gear, bottom is TEAMWORK. Every group view must show both complete humans and all three complete pets. Large readable faces, hands, feet/paws and owl wings/talons; no cropping. No extra actors, creature morphs, generic replacement faces or mixed gear versions. No numbers, costs, capacity/rate claims or implementation approval. Footer AUTHORED UPGRADE PROPOSAL. Natural animal anatomy only; no swords, guns, crossbows, human hands, boots, spiked muzzles or flight-blocking owl armor. Owls retain all visible flight feathers, open shoulder joints and clear talons. Human tools must sit in valid hands or secured sheaths and never pass through bodies. Packs do not create an inventory-capacity upgrade. The actors already work and attack; these are purposeful gear/training improvements, not new basic competence. HEADER HAVENLINE / TRAINED WORK CREW. Gear design: Keep both survivor identities and add distinct practical working protection: the forester/repair worker has a blue armored apron/chest guard and secured tools; the logistics worker has a protected work vest with a real quick-release load fixture. Preserve the dog and wolf scarf/pack identity while adding obvious fitted segmented chest/flank protection and secure quick-release pack mounts. Owl intentionally replaces the bulky bedroll/pouch arrangement with a compact removable flight-load frame and light protective breast shell, retaining face/feathers and blue scarf identity while freeing wing roots and primaries. The rear group view must match all attachments from the front; preserve free joints and reachable tool grips. Bottom teamwork scene: both survivors perform distinct useful jobs, one handling the actual hand-cranked saw/repair position, the other delivering a small visible existing-resource load to a reserved handoff. Keep their physical positions separate and safe. Dog stays beside its protected worker, wolf watches a reachable approach, owl naturally perches with clear wings. Show real object contact and distinct job intent, not a decorative march. No cashier or automatically spawned worker. Existing animal harness/scarf/bedroll/pouches are already present in the supplied base; the upgraded work rig must be visually more useful/protective, not a generic light harness that strips the animal down. Preserve body identity while making the declared modular changes. Use only the supplied selected work object and current resource references in the scene.
